findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the accepted `--only` values in one place (a shared constant or the parser's `choices`) and use it for both the help/argparse choices and the `fsck_cli` validation and error message.
evidence: fsck.py:366: `if only_args[0] != "--only=stale-channel":` (literal duplicated in the error message at 369-370 and 374).
repair.py:51: `choices=("stale-channel",)`.
The original bug was exactly these two definitions drifting apart (help said ticket ids, scan accepted only stale-channel).
findings.finding: The plan doesn't fix the cause of the drift: the accepted `--only` values are defined in two places. `fsck_cli` hard-codes the value check (`only_args[0] != "--only=stale-channel"`), and `build_fsck` separately declares `choices=('stale-channel',)` plus the help string. A test that checks both catches drift after it happens. Deriving the accepted values from one source, such as having the bespoke scan read the parser's `choices` or a shared module-level constant, would stop the two from diverging at all. It is also cheap and limited to the CLI layer. Consider adopting that.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC1 ('a test pins help text and parser behaviour together'); src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:366 vs src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/repair.py:49-53

findings.suggested_fix: Add `FSCK_ONLY_VALUES = ("stale-channel",)` in repair.py. Use it for `choices=` and the help text in `build_fsck`, and in `fsck_cli` check `value not in FSCK_ONLY_VALUES`, building the error message from the same tuple.
